caseResults.title: Prototype Pollution in minimist argument parsing
caseResults.name: minimist

actualFindings.title: Incomplete prototype pollution fix: 'constructor' and 'prototype' path segments are not blocked
actualFindings.recommendation: Don't only compare against '__proto__'. In the traversal loop, reject 'constructor' and 'prototype' as well. Apply the check to the final key assignment too. Better still, only traverse own properties: use Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(o, key), and create intermediate objects with Object.create(null). Alternatively, store the parsed values in a Map or a null-prototype object.

goldenFindings.rationale: Direct traversal of __proto__ key allows remote attackers to pollute Object.prototype

findings.title: Final key of the path is not guarded against '__proto__' or 'constructor' assignment
findings.recommendation: The guard only covers keys[0..n-2]. Apply the same denylist, or an own-property check, to the last key before the assignment. Doing so also stops the final write from altering the prototype or constructor on objects the loop has already reached.

findings.title: Prototype guard leaves constructor.prototype traversal unblocked
findings.recommendation: Reject '__proto__', 'constructor', and 'prototype' in every path segment before traversal or assignment. The new guard permits constructor.prototype traversal through inherited properties, allowing a subsequent assignment to alter Object.prototype.

caseResults.title: Prototype Pollution in ini file section decoding
caseResults.name: ini

actualFindings.title: Incomplete Prototype Pollution Defense Allowing Bypass via 'constructor'
actualFindings.recommendation: Block 'constructor' and 'prototype' in addition to '__proto__', or create the container object with a null prototype using Object.create(null) and defend against prototype property access paths.

goldenFindings.rationale: Unsanitized section key allows __proto__ property injection during INI decoding

findings.title: Incomplete Prototype Pollution Defense Allowing Bypass via 'constructor'
findings.recommendation: Block 'constructor' and 'prototype' in addition to '__proto__', or create the container object with a null prototype using Object.create(null) and defend against prototype property access paths.

findings.title: Prototype pollution guard only matches the exact section name '__proto__'; 'constructor' and dotted-path sections are not covered
findings.recommendation: Block '__proto__', 'constructor' and 'prototype' as section names. Also check every segment of a dotted section name such as '[__proto__.x]' or '[constructor.prototype]' wherever section names are split or walked. Create section containers with Object.create(null), or use Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(out, section) instead of 'out[section] || {}', which returns the inherited Object function for 'constructor'. The diff does not show any later dot-splitting or nesting pass, so confirm in the full ini.js that no such pass can reach Object.prototype.

caseResults.title: Prototype Pollution in JSON-Patch constructor/prototype path
caseResults.name: fast-json-patch

actualFindings.title: Prototype-pollution guard is incomplete: bare 'constructor' and the final path segment are not blocked
actualFindings.recommendation: Reject '__proto__', 'constructor' and 'prototype' as a standalone denylist for every path segment, including the last one (the loop only runs to keys.length - 1). Better, use Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(obj, key) for every traversal step and for the final assignment, and create containers with Object.create(null). Apply the same validation to any 'from' path used by move/copy and to get/remove helpers.

goldenFindings.rationale: Unvalidated constructor/prototype path components allow prototype attribute mutation

findings.title: Prototype guard still permits inherited constructor traversal
findings.recommendation: Reject '__proto__', 'constructor', and 'prototype' in every decoded path segment, including the final segment, before accessing document properties. The path '/constructor/polluted' currently passes this guard and traverses from an ordinary document object into the shared Object constructor.

caseResults.title: ReDoS via greedy whitespace regex in semver
caseResults.name: semver

actualFindings.title: cleanVersion now rejects inputs with more than one leading or trailing whitespace character
actualFindings.recommendation: The original `^\s*...\s*$` is anchored and has no nested quantifiers, so it is not exploitable for ReDoS. Narrowing the whitespace to `\s{0,1}` is not needed for security and changes behavior. Inputs such as '  1.2.3', '1.2.3\n\n' or '\t 1.2.3' used to be accepted and now return null. Either restore `\s*`, or trim the input first and add a length cap (for example `str.length <= 256`) before matching. If the stricter behavior is intended, add tests for it and check the callers.

actualFindings.title: Whitespace limit rejects previously accepted version strings
actualFindings.recommendation: Trim surrounding whitespace before matching an anchored version regex without whitespace quantifiers. Preserve acceptance of inputs such as "  1.2.3" and "1.2.3  ", which now return null instead of "1.2.3".

goldenFindings.rationale: Greedy whitespace quantifier in version parsing regex causes ReDoS
